summary: This study explores the use of optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA) as a non-invasive solution to differentiate Alzheimer's disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and healthy controls (HCs). Retinal parameters extracted from OCT/OCTA examinations were analyzed in 357 participants, revealing significant microvascular density reductions around the fovea in MCI and AD compared to HCs, as well as age-related thickness parameter associations with HCs' old age. Significant thickness/volume reductions in Inner_Retina and Full_Retina layers were also linked to AD and MCI groups.
